According to search-result excerpts of the Issue 9 PDF front matter and the asd-ste100.org downloads/FAQ pages (not opened by this audit because asd-ste100.org returned HTTP 403): no reproduction or publication in whole or in part without written authority of an officer of ASD; receiving a copy confers no licence; named categories (ASD national association members and their member companies, AIA/ICCAIA members, customers of those companies, member-state defence ministries, airworthiness authorities, universities and research institutes for educational purposes) have free irrevocable permission to reproduce or publish; unauthorised distribution directly or via other websites or portals is prohibited without written permission from the STEMG.

provisions.version_examined: OJ L, 2024/2847, 20.11.2024 (original text, English, via Cellar)
provisions.summary: The Regulation covers products with digital elements made available on the market whose intended or reasonably foreseeable use includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection to a device or network.
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers and other economic operators of products with digital elements
provisions.applicable_from: 2027-12-11 (general); see Art. 71(2) for Art. 14 and Chapter IV
provisions.conditions: Excludes products developed exclusively for national security or defence and products designed to process classified information (Art. 2(7), read only as summarised).

provisions.summary: A manufacturer is a person who develops or manufactures a product with digital elements, or has it designed, developed or manufactured, and markets it under its own name or trademark, whether for payment, monetised or free of charge.
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers
provisions.conditions: The reference to free-of-charge supply sits next to the commercial-activity limit in Art. 3(22).

provisions.summary: An open-source software steward is a legal person, other than a manufacturer, whose purpose is to systematically support the development of specific free and open-source products intended for commercial activities, and who ensures those products remain viable.
provisions.applies_to: Foundations and other legal persons that sustain FOSS products intended for commercial use
provisions.conditions: Steward status depends on systematic support of products intended for commercial activities (see recital 19).

provisions.summary: Making available on the market means supplying a product with digital elements for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge.
provisions.applies_to: Scope boundary for FOSS and other products
provisions.conditions: The commercial-activity test is the main route by which non-commercial FOSS falls outside the Regulation; recitals 15 and 18 explain what does and does not count.

provisions.summary: Free and open-source software is software whose source code is openly shared and which is made available under a free and open-source licence granting the rights to freely access, use, modify and redistribute it.
provisions.applies_to: FOSS components and products
provisions.conditions: None stated in the definition itself.

provisions.summary: When integrating components sourced from third parties, a manufacturer must exercise due diligence so that the components do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product; this expressly includes free and open-source components not supplied in a commercial activity.
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers that integrate FOSS or other third-party components
provisions.conditions: Paragraph wording was paraphrased from a model-summarised fetch; Art. 13(4) was later replaced by Regulation (EU) 2025/327 Art. 104 but Art. 13(5) is not listed as changed.

provisions.summary: Manufacturers must notify actively exploited vulnerabilities (para 1) and severe incidents affecting product security (para 3) to the coordinator CSIRT and ENISA through the single reporting platform. For vulnerabilities (para 2) the sequence is early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within 14 days after a corrective measure is available. For severe incidents (para 4) it is early warning within 24 hours, incident notification within 72 hours and a final report within one month of the notification.
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers of in-scope products, including products placed on the market before 2027-12-11 (Art. 69(3))
provisions.conditions: Applies from 2026-09-11 under Art. 71(2); stewards are covered only to the extent set out in Art. 24(3); Art. 14(2)(a)/(4)(a) deadline misses by micro and small enterprises are carved out of fines by Art. 64(10)(a).

provisions.summary: Open-source software stewards must put in place and document in a verifiable manner a cybersecurity policy that fosters secure development and effective vulnerability handling by product developers, encourages voluntary reporting under Art. 15, and promotes sharing of vulnerability information within the open-source community.
provisions.applies_to: Open-source software stewards (Art. 3(14))
provisions.conditions: Light-touch regime; stewards do not affix the CE marking (recital 19).

provisions.summary: Stewards must cooperate with market surveillance authorities on request to mitigate cybersecurity risks of free and open-source products and, on a reasoned request, give the authority the Art. 24(1) documentation in a comprehensible language, on paper or electronically.
provisions.applies_to: Open-source software stewards
provisions.conditions: Triggered by an authority's request.

provisions.summary: Art. 14(1) applies to stewards to the extent they are involved in developing the products; Art. 14(3) and (8) apply to stewards where severe incidents affect network and information systems that the steward provides for the development of the products.
provisions.applies_to: Open-source software stewards
provisions.conditions: Reporting duties are limited to involvement in development or systems the steward provides.

provisions.summary: To support the due-diligence duty in Art. 13(5), the Commission may adopt delegated acts under Art. 61 establishing voluntary security attestation programmes through which developers, users or other third parties can assess whether FOSS products meet all or some of the Regulation's requirements.
provisions.applies_to: Commission (empowerment); developers, users and third parties of FOSS products (voluntary use)
provisions.applicable_from: 2027-12-11 (general); empowerment runs from entry into force
provisions.conditions: Voluntary; no such delegated act was looked for in this audit.

provisions.summary: Manufacturers of products listed in Annex III that qualify as free and open-source software may use any of the conformity assessment procedures in Art. 32(1), including internal control (Module A), provided the technical documentation referred to in Art. 31 is made available to the public when the product is placed on the market.
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers of Annex III important products that are FOSS
provisions.conditions: Condition: public availability of the Art. 31 technical documentation. Regulation (EU) 2025/327 Art. 104 inserts a new Art. 32(5a) for EHR systems.

provisions.citation: Art. 64(10)(b) as corrected by Corrigendum R(02), OJ L 2025/90555 of 2.7.2025
provisions.version_examined: Original OJ text read (says 'paragraphs 3 to 9'); English corrigendum of 2.7.2025 read (corrects to 'paragraphs 2 to 9')
provisions.summary: The administrative fines in paragraphs 2 to 9 (after correction) are not applied to open-source software stewards for any infringement of the Regulation, nor to micro or small enterprises that miss the Art. 14(2)(a) or 14(4)(a) deadlines. Paragraph 2 sets the highest tier (up to EUR 15 million or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover) for breaches of Annex I and Arts 13 and 14.
provisions.applies_to: Open-source software stewards; micro and small enterprises (point (a))
provisions.applicable_from: 2027-12-11 (general application); whether penalties for Art. 14 breaches bite from 2026-09-11 is not stated in the passages read
provisions.conditions: The corrigendum widens the exemption to the paragraph 2 tier; any text read before 2025-07-02 gives the uncorrected range. Member States set the penalty rules (Art. 64(1)); recital 120 (as read) also says stewards are not fined.

provisions.summary: EU type-examination certificates and approval decisions on cybersecurity under other harmonisation legislation stay valid until 2028-06-11 unless they expire earlier or other law says otherwise (para 1). Products placed on the market before 2027-12-11 fall under the Regulation only if they undergo a substantial modification from that date (para 2). Despite para 2, Art. 14 applies to all in-scope products, including those placed on the market before 2027-12-11 (para 3).
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers of products already on the market; certificate holders
provisions.conditions: Substantial modification test; grandfathering of certificates to 2028-06-11.

provisions.summary: The Commission must report on evaluation and review of the Regulation by 2030-12-11 and every four years after, publishing the reports (para 1), and by 2028-09-11 must report, after consulting ENISA and the CSIRTs network, on the single reporting platform in Art. 16 (para 2).
provisions.applies_to: European Commission
provisions.conditions: None beyond consultation in para 2.

provisions.summary: The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal; with publication on 20.11.2024 this is 2024-12-10, which Cellar metadata also records.
provisions.applies_to: All
provisions.conditions: None.

provisions.summary: The Regulation applies from 2027-12-11, except that Art. 14 applies from 2026-09-11 and Chapter IV (Arts 35 to 51) applies from 2026-06-11.
provisions.applies_to: All
provisions.conditions: As of the retrieval date 2026-10-13 the first two dates have passed and the general date has not.

provisions.summary: Describes what counts as supplying a product in the course of a commercial activity, such as charging a price, charging for technical support, monetising through other services, or requiring personal data beyond what is needed for security or interoperability.
provisions.applies_to: Scope determination for all products including FOSS
provisions.applicable_from: Interpretive; follows the Regulation's application dates
provisions.conditions: Recitals are not operative provisions.

provisions.summary: Recital 17 says application to FOSS supplied in a commercial activity should take account of the different FOSS development models. Recital 18 says FOSS is not commercial merely because it is not monetised; a FOSS component is commercial only if its original manufacturer monetises it; financial support, manufacturer contributions or regular releases alone do not make an activity commercial; not-for-profit development is not commercial if all earnings after costs go to not-for-profit objectives; and contributors of source code to FOSS they are not responsible for are outside the Regulation.
provisions.applies_to: FOSS developers, contributors, foundations
provisions.applicable_from: Interpretive; follows the Regulation's application dates
provisions.conditions: Recitals are not operative provisions.

provisions.summary: Recital 19 introduces the light-touch regime for open-source software stewards, legal persons that sustain FOSS development for commercial purposes (including some foundations and not-for-profit entities), with examples such as hosting platforms and source code, governing projects and steering development; stewards do not affix the CE marking to products they support. Recital 20 says hosting software on an open repository or collaboration platform is not by itself making it available on the market; hosting providers are distributors only if they supply it in a commercial activity.
provisions.applies_to: Open-source software stewards; repository and platform hosts
provisions.applicable_from: Interpretive; follows the Regulation's application dates
provisions.conditions: Recitals are not operative provisions.

provisions.summary: Allows the Commission to set up voluntary security attestation programmes for FOSS components not subject to the essential requirements, through a delegated act or a certification scheme under Art. 48 of Regulation (EU) 2019/881; developers, manufacturers, users or public administrations could initiate or finance an attestation.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; FOSS ecosystem
provisions.conditions: Recitals are not operative provisions; operative text is Art. 25.

provisions.summary: Recital 91 says manufacturers of important products that are FOSS may use internal control (Module A) if they make the technical documentation public. Recital 120 says administrative fines are not applied to open-source software stewards for any infringement and Member States should not impose other pecuniary penalties on them.
provisions.applies_to: FOSS manufacturers; open-source software stewards
provisions.conditions: Recital numbers come from model-summarised chunk reads; recital 120 was also described as covering micro and small enterprises missing the 24-hour deadline. Spot-check before verbatim citation.

provisions.version_examined: OJ L, 2025/327, 5.3.2025 (English, via Cellar); end of the article was truncated in the fetch window
provisions.summary: Replaces Art. 13(4) CRA (cybersecurity risk assessment to be part of the technical documentation, may form part of risk assessments required by other Union acts, with justification where essential requirements do not apply), replaces Art. 31(3) CRA (a single combined technical documentation set where other Union acts also require it), and inserts Art. 32(5a) CRA (manufacturers of EHR systems under Regulation (EU) 2025/327 demonstrate conformity with Annex I through the Chapter III conformity assessment procedure).
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers of products with digital elements, in particular EHR systems
provisions.applicable_from: Not confirmed; EHDS general application date is 2027-03-26 (Art. 105(2)) and no specific date for Art. 104 was seen
provisions.conditions: Third amendment text cut off in the fetch window.

provisions.summary: Enters into force on the twentieth day after publication (2025-03-25 per Cellar) and applies from 2027-03-26, with phased dates of 2029-03-26 and 2031-03-26 for particular articles and data categories, and 2035-03-26 for Art. 75(5).
provisions.applies_to: All EHDS actors
provisions.conditions: Phases depend on data category and article.
